annotations.annotation_text: The Letter motif "parchment" on page 395 ("Tristan and Isolde"): ALP's mysterious document — scratched from the midden by Biddy Doran the Hen — represents the genesis of all writing within the voyage of Tristan and Isolde observed by the Four Old Men as seagulls, Wagnerian chromatic motifs, King Mark's displacement. During this Age of Heroes (closing) phase, the letter functions simultaneously as archaeological artifact, love note, legal deposition, and the text of Finnegans Wake itself.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Deane, Vincent, et al. The Finnegans Wake Notebooks at Buffalo. https://www.brepols.net

annotations.annotation_text: Liturgical echo "Amen" on page 395 ("Tristan and Isolde"): Catholic ritual, Latin prayer, and sacramental language weave through the voyage of Tristan and Isolde observed by the Four Old Men as seagulls, Wagnerian chromatic motifs, King Mark's displacement. Joyce fuses ecclesiastical solemnity with domestic banality during the Age of Heroes (closing) phase, treating the tavern counter as communion rail and the sleeping body as sacred vessel.
sources: Contemporary Literature Press: Classical Lexicon for FW. https://editura.mttlc.ro
Frazer, Sir James George. Folk-Lore in the Old Testament. https://archive.org/details/folkloreinoldtes01frazuoft
